title: PREDICTING ENERGY DISSIPATION EFFICIENCY IN RECTANGULAR SHARP-CRESTED WEIRS: A TECHNICAL SOLUTION FOR WATER FLOW CONTROL

PREDICTING ENERGY DISSIPATION EFFICIENCY IN RECTANGULAR SHARP-CRESTED WEIRS: A TECHNICAL SOLUTION FOR WATER FLOW CONTROL

Journal: Water Conservation and Management (WCM)
Author: Afrah A.Alkraidi, Ayam Jabbar Jihad, Mariam Qasim

ABSTRACT

This study investigates the energy dissipation efficiency of rectangular sharp-crested weirs with different heights under various flow conditions. Three weir heights were tested to evaluate the effect of weir height on energy dissipation within the tested range. The experimental results showed that the energy dissipation ratio (EDR) decreases with increasing flow discharge, while the residual energy increases. Weir height significantly affects EDR, with higher weirs exhibiting greater energy dissipation efficiency within the experimental conditions. An empirical model based on dimensionless parameters was developed to predict EDR and residual energy, showing good agreement between predicted and observed values. The proposed model achieved a coefficient of determination (R² = 0.935). The applicability of the model is limited to the tested range of hydraulic conditions.
